title: A parity-corrected potential proves the Elsholtz–Klahn–Lipnik four-term progression-free digit-set conjecture
exact_endpoint: Digits356756.mathdb_356756 : for p prime, 13 <= p, p % 4 = 1, (p+3)/2 | n, there are no a b c d : Fin n -> ZMod p in SourceSet p n with zero second differences and a != b; Digits356756.no_affine_progression : no x + j r (j in Fin 4, r != 0) lies in SourceSet p n
scope: Elsholtz-Klahn-Lipnik (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 91 (2023) 1443-1452, arXiv:2211.02588) Conjecture 2.4, repeated as Conjecture 4.6 in Lipnik's 2023 thesis: for every prime p >= 13, p = 1 mod 4, and every n divisible by (p+3)/2, S(D,n) with D = {0..(p-1)/2,(p+3)/2} has no nonconstant 4-term AP. Proved uniformly (primality unnecessary) via E(t) = 4t^2 - (3p-5)(-1)^t: the only wrapped coordinate progressions are (h-3,0,h,3) and (3,h,0,h-3), with gap 16; ordinary progressions have gap 16 s^2; equal digit frequencies force every gap to vanish.
source_targets: C. Elsholtz, B. Klahn, G. F. Lipnik, arXiv:2211.02588v1 Conjecture 2.4; Des. Codes Cryptogr. 91 (2023) 1443-1452
substantive_reason: Fully resolves an explicitly posed published conjecture, uniformly in p and n. The source verified it only computationally for p <= 31 through its ILP model. The decisive ingredient, the parity-corrected potential with the complete wrap classification, appears in neither the source nor its cited works, and the classical quadratic potential provably fails (gap -120 at p = 13). It is not a bridge from the source's own lemmas.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; not worldwide priority
remaining_literature_limits: arXiv listing coverage for late 2026 bounded (one listing timed out; not retried)
trust_limits: Stirling cardinality consequence and EHPS comparison are ordinary mathematics, not formalized
not_claimed: A new record lower bound for r_4(Z_p^n) (EHPS 2406.12290 gives a larger base for p >= 41; source Table 1 has a larger set at p = 29)
